transcript:
--- Meeting header ---
Date: 2025-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (BrightCart - Head of Search), Tom Reynolds (BrightCart - Eng Manager), Priya Shah (BrightCart - Data Scientist)

--- Auto summary (generated) ---
Quick demo of hosted embeddings + rerank flow: create embeddings for corpus, store in vector DB, candidate retrieval + Redwood rerank endpoint for final ordering. Highlight: streaming, per-route cost visibility in Console, and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Lena, AE at Redwood, with Marco our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Sara Kim: Good, hi. Excited to see the embeddings / rerank demo, we've been fighting relevance for a bit.
00:10 Marco Diaz: Great, we'll demo the hosted API flow first - embeddings to retrieve candidates then call the rerank endpoint to rescore. I'll share my screen in a sec.
00:25 Tom Reynolds: Quick context - we have ~12 million product SKUs, latency target is <150ms P95 for search, budget is tight so cost per query matters. We currently use Elastic and a small vector layer.
00:40 Marco Diaz: Okay great, that helps. So typical Redwood hosted flow: call /embeddings to vectorize queries and docs, we recommend 768-1536 dims depending on model; store vectors in your store (we integrate with common vector DBs). For rerank, our /rerank endpoint takes a query and a list of candidate documents and returns an ordered list with scores, you can run it as a second-pass to boost relevance.
01:05 Sara Kim: Are the embeddings models fixed? Can we pick open models?
01:09 Marco Diaz: Yes you can pick from our catalog - we support multiple open models and provide Redwood-verified performance profiles. You can also pin a model version. Slight mispronounce - not versioning.
01:20 Priya Shah: Do you support batching and async? We have spikes on Black Friday-like events.
01:25 Marco Diaz: Yes, Redwood Optimize suggests batching policies; the serving runtime does continuous batching and KV cache helps for repeated prefixes. For spikes we have autoscaling on Dedicated; for hosted there's burst capacity and smart routing.
01:45 Lena Park: I'll show the Console quickly - per-route latency, token costs, and the Optimize tab where recommendations appear. Marco can demo the API call sequence.
02:10 Marco Diaz: Ok screen share. Here's a sample request: POST /v1/embeddings with {"model":"redwood-embed-1", "input":"red running shoes"} then response with vector. You store vector in your DB. For retrieval we do ANN but you can use your own index. Then second step: POST /v1/rerank with payload {"query":"red running shoes","candidates": [{"id": "123","text":"..."}, ...]} - we return scores + normalized ranks.
03:00 Tom Reynolds: What's the average latency for a rerank call for say 10 candidates?
03:05 Marco Diaz: For hosted with our smaller rerank model it's typically 25-50ms per request at p50 for 10 candidates, p95 varies with seq length. If you need ultra-low latency we recommend quantized dedicated variants. These numbers are estimates; we'll run benchmarks with your corpus.
03:30 Sara Kim: How does cost look? We're paying per token for generation profiles - how do rerank/embeddings charge?
03:35 Lena Park: Embeddings are billed per vector unit (per 1K tokens-ish), rerank is per request and depends on model size / candidate count. We'll send a sample pricing sheet - Marco will include typical unit economics for our common configs.
04:00 Priya Shah: Security - are logs retained? We have PCI-ish constraints for payment-adjacent metadata.
04:05 Lena Park: Hosted retains logs by default but you can configure retention. We offer Private (VPC / on-prem) for regulated workloads and we have KMS integrations for key control. We also have SOC2 and audit logs; I'll attach the pack.
04:30 Tom Reynolds: Do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC in Console?
04:33 Lena Park: Yes SSO, role-based access controls, and audit trails are supported. Enterprise tier.
05:00 Marco Diaz: Back to rerank - couple of patterns: 1) Re-rank top-K from ANN with our endpoint, 2) Signal-fusion where you pass features along (e.g., clicks, recency) as metadata and the reranker uses them, 3) Hybrid where you score candidate syntactically first.
05:40 Sara Kim: Can the reranker accept additional metadata per candidate? We want recency and business-priority flags.
05:45 Marco Diaz: Yep, you can send additional fields in the candidate object; we'll surface them to the model. Note: feature engineering helps - the reranker doesn't magically know business constraints unless you pass them.
06:10 Priya Shah: Could we see an example notebook or a reference implementation?
06:15 Marco Diaz: Sure, I'll share a demo notebook after call - shows ingestion, vectorization, ANN retrieval, rerank call, and eval metrics like MRR/NDCG.
06:30 Sara Kim: How do you measure regressions when we change models? We need quality gating.
06:35 Lena Park: Redwood Optimize ties evals to prompt sets and regression alerts. You can run offline evals on holdout queries and we can alert on drops in metrics.
07:00 Tom Reynolds: Ok demo time.
07:05 Marco Diaz: I'll run a live example - query "waterproof trail running shoes". First embeddings call... (typing noises) returned vector. Then ANN top-100, then rerank top-10. Results show boosted items that match technical specs and user reviews.
09:20 Sara Kim: Nice, looks like the rerank prioritized items with "membrane" and "sealed seams" which is good.
09:40 Marco Diaz: Sometimes transcripts have slight lag here - on real traffic the KV cache helps with repeated queries.
10:00 Priya Shah: For evaluation, how should we sample negatives?
10:05 Marco Diaz: Typical is hard negatives from lexical search and random negatives. Our notebook includes harvested negatives and evaluation harness.
11:00 Tom Reynolds: If we start with hosted, can we later move to Dedicated or Private without changing code?
11:05 Lena Park: Yes that's a core Redwood promise - same API and config across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. Moving to VPC/private may require some config but API surface remains consistent.
11:35 Sara Kim: Any known issues with large SKU counts? We have 12M vectors, cost of ANN storage is a concern.
11:45 Marco Diaz: Storage cost is separate - Redwood doesn't force a particular vector DB; you can use cloud-managed vector DBs optimized for cost or host in your infra. Optimize can recommend dimension reduction or quantization to save storage / compute.
12:10 Priya Shah: Can you do on-device or on-prem quantized models?
12:15 Marco Diaz: For Private deployments we support quantized runtimes and can recommend kernels. That said, hosted uses our optimized kernels and supports quantized model variants too.
12:40 Sara Kim: What about A/B tests and rollouts? We want to test rerank model changes.
12:45 Lena Park: Console supports canary rollouts and A/B with metrics; you can route a percentage of traffic to new rerank config and Redwood will surface per-route metrics.
13:10 Tom Reynolds: Any pitfalls with cold-start latency?
13:15 Marco Diaz: Cold starts mostly for larger models; persistent workers and warm pools mitigate. For bursty traffic, KV caching reduces repeated token compute.
13:45 Priya Shah: How deterministic are rerank scores? We need stable ordering for logs.
13:50 Marco Diaz: You can set temperature=0 for deterministic behavior; rerank models are often tuned to be consistent. Note: small nondeterminism can occur with floating point and distributed serving but it's usually negligible.
14:20 Sara Kim: Could Redwood host our vector DB?
14:25 Lena Park: We don't currently host customer vector DBs full-managed; we integrate with partners and you can host in your account. For Dedicated we can offer tighter integrations.
14:50 Tom Reynolds: Let's talk about P95 targets - do you have concrete numbers for 95th percentile with 10 candidates and typical payload?
14:55 Marco Diaz: We'll run an apples-to-apples benchmark with your data. In-house numbers: embeddings ~30-80ms depending on model; rerank for 10 candidates ~40-120ms p95 on shared hosted. For Dedicated you can see 20-40ms p95 for small rerank models. We'll validate with the POC.
15:30 Sara Kim: Regarding data retention again - are request/response logs encrypted at rest?
15:35 Lena Park: Yes encrypted at rest with KMS; for hosted customers we manage keys unless you use customer-managed keys in Private.
16:00 Priya Shah: Will you accept our anonymized logs for the benchmark? We need to scrub user IDs.
16:05 Lena Park: Absolutely, please remove PII. We'll also sign an NDA if needed.
16:30 Marco Diaz: Quick note on rerank inputs size - passing long candidate texts increases latency; you can pass condensed excerpts or metadata to keep payload small. We often store full text in your DB and pass snippets.
17:00 Tom Reynolds: Any limit on candidate count per rerank call?
17:05 Marco Diaz: Hosted has soft limits; recommend re-ranking top 10-50. Larger candidate sets increase compute linearly. We'll discuss in POC.
17:30 Sara Kim: What about streaming responses and function calling - not relevant but curious.
17:35 Lena Park: Streaming is mostly for generation; rerank returns a single scored payload so streaming isn't typical. Function calling is supported in other endpoints.
18:00 Priya Shah: Are there examples that combine click-through rate features?
18:05 Marco Diaz: Yes the demo notebook includes click features and shows improved NDCG; we can adapt to your telemetry schema.
19:00 Tom Reynolds: I'm worried about vendor lock-in. If we move to another provider how hard to extract models/rollouts?
19:05 Lena Park: We try to avoid lock-in - standard APIs, you control vectors and can export logs and model configs. But inevitably some infra differences exist.
19:40 Sara Kim: Ok let's talk timeline - we want a POC in the next two weeks. Is that feasible?
19:45 Lena Park: Yes, propose 1-week POC starting 2025-08-28: ingest samples, run benchmarks, and share results. We'll provide a small team and scripts.
20:05 Marco Diaz: I'll run an offline benchmark and show MRR/NDCG improvements and cost per query.
20:30 Priya Shah: Any recommendations for embeddings dimension? We use 384 in a legacy flow.
20:35 Marco Diaz: 384 is fine but larger dims may give better semantic fidelity; Optimize can recommend based on your eval set. For cost tradeoff, 384 -> cheaper storage and slightly faster retrieval.
21:00 Tom Reynolds: Do you have a sandbox key or trial credits?
21:05 Lena Park: Yes we offer free credits for POC and a sandbox API key, we'll provision after NDA.
21:35 Sara Kim: Great. Can you send the sample spreadsheet for rerank benchmarks?
21:40 Marco Diaz: On it.
22:00 Lena Park: Recap: we'll send pricing/security pack, Marco shares demo notebook + benchmark sheet, BrightCart will upload anonymized logs, and we'll schedule POC kickoff. Any other questions?
22:20 Tom Reynolds: Not right now, looks good.
22:30 Sara Kim: Thanks everyone.
22:40 Lena Park: Thanks all - we'll follow up with notes and links.

--- End transcript ---
